verses.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਭਾਉ ਤਿਨ ਨਾਹਿ ਭਉ ਮੁਚੁ ਭਉ ਅਗੈ ਨਿਭਵਿਆਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: jinhaa(n) bhaau tin naeh bhau much bhau agai nibhaviaahaa|

en.bdb: They are not scared of anybody who have cherished the love of the Lord and those who are devoid of the fear of Lord remain scared in the court of Lord.

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਗਿ ਤਤੀ ਜਲ ਸੀਅਲਾ ਨਿਵ ਚਲੈ ਸਿਰੁ ਕਰੈ ਉਤਾਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: ag tatee jal seealaa niv chalai sir karai utaahaa|

en.bdb: Since it keeps its head high, the fire is hot and because the water flows downwards, it is cold.

verses.gurmukhi: ਭਰਿ ਡੁਬੈ ਖਾਲੀ ਤਰੈ ਵਜਿ ਨ ਵਜੈ ਘੜੈ ਜਿਵਾਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: bhar ddubai khaalee tarai vaj na vajai ghaRai jivaahaa|

en.bdb: The filled up pitcher drowns and makes no sound and the empty one not only goes on swimming, it rather makes the noise also (likewise is the egotist and the egoless one, the latter absorbing in loving devotion gets liberated and the former goes on tossing

verses.gurmukhi: ਅੰਬੁ ਸੁਫਲ ਫਲਿ ਝੁਕਿ ਲਹੈ ਦੁਖ ਫਲੁ ਅਰੰਡੁ ਨ ਨਿਵੈ ਤਲਾਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: a(n)b sufal fal jhuk lahai dhukh fal ara(n)dd na nivai talaahaa|

en.bdb: Being full of fruits, the mango tree bends down in humility but the castor tree being full of bitter fruits never bows in humility.

verses.gurmukhi: ਮਨੁ ਪੰਖੇਰੂ ਧਾਵਦਾ ਸੰਗਿ ਸੁਭਾਇ ਜਾਇ ਫਲ ਖਾਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: man pa(n)kheroo dhaavadhaa sa(n)g subhai jai fal khaahaa|

en.bdb: The mind-bird keeps flying and according to its nature picks up the fruits.

verses.gurmukhi: ਧਰਿ ਤਾਰਾਜੂ ਤੋਲੀਐ ਹਉਲਾ ਭਾਰਾ ਤੋਲੁ ਤੁਲਾਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: dhar taaraajoo toleeaai haulaa bhaaraa tol tulaahaa|

en.bdb: On the scale of justice, the light and the heavy are weighed (and good and bad are differentiated).

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਿਣਿ ਹਾਰੈ ਹਾਰੈ ਜਿਣੈ ਪੈਰਾ ਉਤੇ ਸੀਸੁ ਧਰਾਹਾ।
verses.translit_en: jin haarai haarai jinai pairaa ute sees dharaahaa|

en.bdb: He who looks to be winning here loses in the court of the Lord and likewise the loser here wins there.
All bow at his feet. The individual first falls at the feet (of Guru) and then he makes all to fall at his feet.
